name: North East Rail Trail (Scottsdale → Billycock Hill)
length_time: 26 km one way (shorter 3, 9, 12, 16 km sections); walk 6–8 hrs full length
features: Compacted gravel, max 3% grade. Farmland, bush, tree-fern cuttings, Great Forester River. Wallabies, pademelons, echidnas. Toilets at Scottsdale, Tonganah, Legerwood; picnic shelters.
notes: Starts in town at the Scottsdale Railway Precinct. Keep dog clear of livestock; watch for snakes in warmer months.

name: Scottsdale off-lead area (18 Christopher St)
features: Council land where dogs can run off lead all year – good for a stretch after the drive from Devonport.
notes: Children's Reserve & Memorial Park are dog-free; Northeast Park is on lead only.

name: Mt Stronach Summit
features: Peppermint & stringybark forest, granite slabs, panoramic views over the north-east, 1903 Federation cairn at the top.
notes: In Mt Stronach Regional Reserve – regional reserves usually allow dogs on a lead, but no official dog statement found. Check signage at the trailhead.

name: Hollybank Reserve forest walk (Underwood)
features: Educational forest walk with interpretive signs, picnic grounds. Handy leg-stretch on the Launceston–Scottsdale drive.
notes: Just off the Tasman Hwy on the Devonport → Scottsdale leg.

name: Bridport Walking Track + Adams Beach
features: River, forest, foreshore and wildflower sections; secluded beaches; Aboriginal heritage. Adams Beach allows dogs OFF lead all year.
notes: Wildflower Reserve: on lead 6am–7pm. Dogs prohibited on the foreshore east of the track from Granite Point to Anderson Bay. Eastmans/Goftons beaches on lead 1 Apr–1 Nov.

name: Goblin Forest Walk (Blue Tier, Poimena)
features: Moss-covered myrtle rainforest, old tin-mining relics, alpine plateau car park at Poimena.
notes: ~9 km gravel up from Weldborough. Can be cold/foggy – take a jacket.

name: Moon Valley Rim (Blue Tier, Poimena)
length_time: Sources vary: 3 km / ~2 hrs to 10 km
features: Circuit around the rim below Mt Poimena with valley and mountain views across the Blue Tier.
notes: Same car park as Goblin Forest – pair them. Confirm route length at the trailhead.

name: Beaumaris Beach North (opposite Paddys Island)
length_time: Long beach walk – as far as you like
features: Long stretch of east-coast sand facing Paddys Island; 24-hour dog beach.
notes: Right at your base. Check Break O'Day Council dog-zone signs for seasonal changes.

name: Scamander Beach / Four Mile Creek / Mariposa Point
features: Scamander river mouth, surf beach and rocky points just south of Beaumaris. Council off-lead area.
notes: Seasonal restrictions can apply near bird-breeding zones – check BODC dog-zones map.

name: St Helens foreshore (Stieglitz & Georges Bay)
features: Waterfront path around Georges Bay, cafés and fish-and-chips in town. St Helens also has an off-lead area.
notes: On the route in from Scottsdale.

name: Humbug Point Loop
features: Nature recreation area on Georges Bay – orange-lichen granite, quiet coves, birdlife, coastal heath.
notes: Parks & Wildlife confirm dogs on leads permitted.

name: Peron Dunes
features: Huge sand dunes and beach at the mouth of Georges Bay.
notes: Listed as dog-friendly; 4WDs use the area. Check BODC dog-zone map for current lead rules.

name: Bay of Fires – Cosy Corner, Swimcart Lagoon, Suicide Beach
features: The famous white sand, turquoise water and orange-lichen granite boulders.
notes: Dog access can be seasonal due to shorebird nesting. Don't go north into Mt William National Park – no dogs.

name: Mt Gnomon (Penguin)
features: Lush and eucalypt forest above Penguin – a good break on the long north-west coast drive.
notes: Between Devonport and Burnie.

name: Hellyer Beach (Port Latta)
features: Quiet beach and river mouth just off the Bass Hwy between Wynyard and Smithton.
notes: Listed as dog-friendly; check local signs for lead rules.

name: Edge of the World (Gardiner Point)
features: Viewing platform where the Arthur River meets the wild Southern Ocean; huge driftwood logs; BBQ & toilets.
notes: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area – dogs on leads permitted.

name: Arthur River Coastal Walk (river mouth → Church Rock)
features: Wild windswept coastline north from the river mouth to Church Rock – rocks, beaches, big seas.
notes: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area – dogs on leads permitted.

name: Bluff Hill Point
features: Coastal lookout with beach access and lighthouse, just north of Arthur River.
notes: On the road in from Marrawah/Smithton.

name: Petroglyphs Coastal Walk – Sundown Point
features: Old 4WD track then beach, dolerite cliffs, ~2,000-year-old Aboriginal rock carvings.
notes: Start near Nelson Bay campground (ask the Arthur River Parks office for directions). Significant Aboriginal site – stay on track, keep dog close.

name: Strahan Historic Foreshore Walk
features: Macquarie Harbour waterfront with galleries and history pillars; dog-friendly cafés nearby (Coffee Shack, Risby Cove).

name: Hogarth Falls (People's Park)
features: Tall gums and temperate rainforest along Botanical Creek to the falls; platypus sometimes seen.
notes: One of Tasmania's 60 Great Short Walks.

name: Ocean Beach
features: Tasmania's longest beach – wild surf and famous sunsets.
notes: On or off lead per West Coast tourism. Keep dogs away from the shearwater rookery (Sep–Apr). Not safe for swimming.

name: Ocean Beach Trail
features: Low-impact trail shared with bikes and horses.

name: Henty Dunes
features: Giant sand dunes up to ~30 m; sandboarding, picnic area.
notes: On the Zeehan Rd you drive in on. Reported dog-friendly by Dog Friendly Tasmania – check signs.

name: Montezuma Falls (near Rosebery)
features: Old railway formation through rainforest to a 104 m waterfall; swing bridge, mine relics.
notes: Detour from Zeehan (not on the Western Explorer). Worth a half-day.

name: Horsetail Falls (Queenstown)
features: Boardwalk to a seasonal 50 m waterfall with mountain views over the Queenstown moonscape.
notes: Steps and drop-offs – keep dog close.

name: St Columba Falls
features: 90 m waterfall in rainforest near Pyengana.
notes: State Reserve – dogs not permitted.

name: Mt William National Park
features: Northern end of the Bay of Fires.
notes: National Park – dogs not permitted. Stay south of the park boundary.

name: Trowutta Arch
features: Collapsed-cave arch and sinkhole in the Tarkine.
notes: Confirmed no dogs (Discover the Tarkine).

name: West Point State Reserve
features: Big surf, Aboriginal heritage.
notes: State Reserve – dogs not permitted.

name: Nelson Falls
features: Popular falls on the Lyell Hwy.
notes: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park – dogs not permitted.
